This 
 document out lines the major maintenance procedure P1, which must performed 
 every five years as indicated by Y5 in the title block.

Regenerative Air Heater used for saving heat from flue gasses and use this 
 heat for heating combustion air to increase boiler efficiency

The 
 first draft initiated by eng. Abdalla Mohamed Abdalla, 
 reviewed by director eng. Gamal Mahmoud Ahmed Arafa, revised by EDEPC quality control eng. Samir Abd el-Gelil, 
 accepted by general director eng. Mohamed Abd El-Salam Mahmoud, approved by eng: Michael Goerge: 
 head sector of Ayoun Moussa steam power station 2x320 MW, and certified by

sections.text:
Disassembly of Heat 
Transfer Surface in Semi-Modular Air Preheaters

items: Remove rotor housing basket installation/removal door.

Rotate the rotor to line up the basket opening in the rotor with the basket 
 installation/removal opening in the housing panel.
Unbolt reversible pulley and install on the top side of the movable platform.

Cut loose welds between the rotor 
 structure (diaphragms and rotor shell) and the axial seal bars and the 
 adjustable circumferential basket seal angles.

Hook the "Tugger" cable to the cold side 
 basket cover frame and pull baskets out of rotor . Repeat this step until all 
 baskets have been removed from the layer.
Adjust basket platform to level of next layer and repeat steps 4 and 5.

Repeat steps 4 through 6 until all heat transfer surface is removed from the 
 semi-modular rotor compartment.

Rotate the rotor to the full sector closest to opposite of the last unloaded 
 sector and repeat steps 4 through 7.

Repeat steps 4 through 8 until all heat transfer surface has been removed from 
 the semi-modular rotor.

Unthread the 'Tugger" cable through the 
 pulleys. Unbolt the reversible pulley and install on the bottom side of the 
 movable platform. Thread the "Tugger" 
 cable through pulley's.

sections.text:
Rotor Seal Assembly, Replacement 
and Setting Fig 1, 2

items:
Remove present radial seals and holding strips. It may be necessary to burn or 
 twist bolts off to remove seals ... etc

When installing the new seals start at the outboard end by inserting bolts 
 along with washers in outboard and inboard bolt holes of outboard seal. The 
 bolts are to be inserted in the trailing edge of the diaphragms

Install radial seal section and secure with nuts and washers. Do not tighten 
 but what seal may be moved in or out as required for final setting
Install remaining bolts and washers in this section

Repeat this procedure for the inboard radial seal leaf section to clear the 
 rotor post seal.

After new seals have been installed on all diaphragms, install seal straight 
 edge assembly by bolting to support channels which have been welded, one 
 inboard and one outboard in either the gas or air side of the hot and cold 
 connecting plates

Rotate the rotor such that the seals of one diaphragm are at the edge of a 
 sector plate. By use of a feeler gauge set the inner and outer seals to the 
 specified clearance and tighten the nuts

Rotate rotor such that seals are at edge of opposite sector plate. Check 
 clearance from sector plate inboard and outboard. If the variation in 
 clearance is not greater than
 .020" (0.5 mm) no further adjustment 
 in seal setting is required

If the variation is greater than 0.20" (0.5 mm) reset the seals to the 
 specified clearance from the sector plate having the largest clearance from 
 the diaphragm using the clearances given on seal setting chart

Rotate rotor such that diaphragm with the seals which have been set to the 
 sector plate is located under seal straight edge. Adjust straight edge so that 
 it just contacts seal and secure

Rotate rotor such that seals of each diaphragm are located under straight 
 edge. Adjust seal leaves so that they just contact the straight edge and 
 secure

After all redial seals have been set to straight edge and secured, remove 
 straight edge and store for future use

For access to the axial seals, remove the covers from seal access openings 
 which are located each side of the main pedestals

Remove present axial seal leaves and holding strips by removing nuts which 
 secure these components

Install axial seal straight edge which is bolted to channels which have been 
 welded to the inside of the rotor housing adjacent to the axial seal plate at 
 both hot and cold end

Set straight edge such that it is 3/16" (5mm) from point of maximum horizontal 
 A run out of pin rack rail and rotor sealing angle. These points may be 
 determined and marked by rotating the rotor by a stationary pointer

Install holding strips and seal leaves and secure with nuts and washers. Do 
 not tighten but what seal leaves may be moved in or out as required for final 
 adjustment

Rotate rotor such that axial seal is located under straight edge. Adjust seal 
 leaves so that they just contact straight edge and secure

Install holding strips and axial seal leaves on remaining diaphragms, setting 
 the seals to the straight edge

Proceed to check and reset axial seal plates, if necessary, by rotating rotor 
 until the axial seals of one diaphragm are at edge of axial seal plate. Refer 
 to the seal setting chart by use of feeler gauge check the clearance from the 
 axial seal to the axial seal plate at both hot and cold end. If it does not 
 vary more than .020" ( 0.5 mm) no adjustment of the axial seal 
 plates is required

If the variation is greater than the .020" ( 0.5 mm) move axial seal plate 
 in or out by use of the adjusters which are located exterior of the air 
 preheater in the main pedestal to obtain the specified clearance

Rotate rotor such that axial seal is at exit edge of axial seal plate and 
 check clearance. If the variation from specified setting is greater than 
 .020" ( 0.5 mm) adjust axial seal plate to obtain required clearance at hot 
 and cold ends

Rotate rotor such that axial seal is at opposite axial seal plate. Follow 
 above procedure in checking the clearances and adjustment of axial seal plate, 
 if required
Replace axial seal access covers

The bypass seals are bolted to the by-pass seal angle which is attached to the 
 connecting plate flange. These seals run from sector plate to sector plate on 
 both the gas and air side at the hot and cold ends. Access to these seals is 
 from the inside of the air preheater. To replace these seals remove the 
 present seals and holding strips. Retain the holding strips for use with the 
 new seals. It may be necessary to burn or twist bolts off to remove seals.

When installing the new seals make sure you have the proper width seals. When 
 installing the new seals make sure that the outer leaves stagger the inner 
 leaves such that the bend slots are not exposed. It will be necessary to trim 
 the seal leaves to fit against the axial seal plates and sector plates. It may 
 also be necessary to trim one or more

Of the outer seal leaves to maintain bolt hole alignment. When installing the 
 new seals it is important that they be correctly positioned on the pin rack 
 and rotor sealing angle to avoid run off during operation. At the cold end, 
 the top of the seal leaves should be 1/2"-1"(13-19mm) from the bottom of the 
 pin rack rail.

Refer to the seal setting chart in this section of the O & M manual for the 
 specified clearance between the bypass seals and sealing surfaces at both the 
 hot and cold end. 
 The seal leaves may have to be sprung in or out, to obtain this clearance.

It is seldom necessary to replace the rotor post seals. However, if the 
 occasion should arise, remove the present seals which are seal welded to the 
 diaphragms and lugs and grind off the welds

When installing the new seals make sure 4543 you have the correct width seal. 
 The seal for the cold end is wider than the hot end seal.

The seals for each respective end are furnished in four 90 degree sections and 
 are notched to fit over the inboard end of the diaphragms

When installing the rotor post seals make sure you have 1/4" (6mm) clearance 
 between the seal and the horizontal sealing surface. You should also have 
 1/16" (2mm) clearance between the seal and the vertical sealing surface. The 
 seal sections are to be welded at the joints and seal welded to the lugs and 
 diaphragms only.
Drain oil from bearing housing.

Remove bearing housing cover. (Splits to be match 
 marked.)

Disconnect and remove thermocouple and 
 thermostat
Remove oil lines from bearing housing
Remove bearing housing; hold down bolts

Raise bearing housing by use of jacking bolts 
 until load is removed from mounting pads and shims. Keep each set of pads and 
 shims together and note location from which they were removed for reinstallation

Lower bearing housing using jacking bolts until 
 it contacts the support plate in center section.

Install safety eye 
 bolt (swivel type) to bearing housing

Slide bearing housing from underneath rotor post 
 until it is in an accessible location for removal and replacement
Remove bolts and retainer plate from stub shaft

Remove bearing from stub shaft and runner bore. A 
 puller may be used if necessary. Use extreme care so that surface of runner 
 will not be scratched or gouged

Clean bearing surface at end of stub shaft and 
 bore of runner

Apply a coat of light oil to inner and outer race 
 of new bearing and install on end of stub shaft and in runner bore. Jacking 
 bolts may be used between O.D. runner and
 I.D. bearing housing to center runner so 
 that radial bearing will slide easily into place. 
 Install retainer 
 plate and tighten bolts evenly and incrementally 
 to 150 ft/lbs. (204
 nm) torque
Position bearing housing under rotor post

Raise bearing housing evenly using 
 jacking bolts until runner and flange of rotor post are seated. Check with 
 feeler gauge

Reinstall mounting pads and shims in same 
 location as they were prior to removal

Install bearing housing hold down bolts. Do not 
 tighten

Lower jacking bolts until bearing housing rests 
 on mounting pads

Using a precision level on top of bearing 
 housing, check level of housing "Reshim" if necessary

Tighten bearing housing hold down bolts to 660-690 
 ft./lbs. (895-935 
 nm) torque

Remove blocks and lower rotor using jacks until 
 runner and rotor post flange are fully seated

Remove jacks and reinstall static spool segments 
 removed for access to jack rotor

Install oil suction line, oil inlet linen and 
 dipstick
Install thermocouple and thermostat
Fill bearing housing to proper level with new oil

Install bearing housing cover using a sealant 
 between splits and also at area where cover bolts to 
 trunnion flange
Block guide trunnion to prevent movement
Drain oil from bearing housing
disconnect water piping to heat exchanger
Remove bolts which secure bearing housing cover to bearing housing

Using a sling and eye bolts provided for this purpose, remove bearing housing 
 cover along with the oil circulating system with internal discharge and 
 suction lines attached
Remove radial bearing ring
Remove bars which lock bolts that secure locking cap to top of trunnion Loosen bolts and back out 3/8" (9.5 mm).

Remove the pipe plug from the center of the trunnion 
 and connect a hydraulic pressure. ram having 5,000-10,000 psi (170 K/m2 
 - 340 K/m2) capacity. Using 
 hydraulic pressure, break the adapter sleeve loose. After breaking the 
 adapter sleeve loose remove the locking cap bolts and locking cap

Using a sling along with eye bolts in the adapter sleeve remove the adapter 
 sleeve and bearing

Remove the bearing from the adapter sleeve by first removing the SKF lock plate and back off locknut approximately 3/16" (4.8 mm). 
 Hydraulic pressure may now be employed to break bearing loose from sleeve by 
 connecting pressure hose to tapped hole in end of adapter sleeve
Once bearing has broken loose remove locknut and bearing from adapter sleeve
Force new bearing on adapter sleeve using the locknut and simultaneously

Position guide bearing assembly unit over trunnion 
 using sling and eye bolts in adapter sleeve

Lower unit down on trunnion. Install locking cap 
 at top of trunnion.
Reinstall radial bearing ring

Install housing cover and circulating system making sure that packing under 
 cover is in proper position
Fill housing to proper level with recommended lubricant

 Air Preheater

Jack selection data and
 Recommended 
 Jacking Procedure

Rrecommended 
 Jacking Procedure 
 Unbolt and remove section from trunnion spool for access to end of rotor 
 post
 Position jacks or rams on jack supports so that when elevated they will 
 contact the rotor post headers
 Raise jacks or rams until they contact the rotor post headers

Determine dimension between rotor post header and jack support. Obtain 
 (four) 4* (102mm) diameter or rectangular bars of this dimension and install 
 adjacent to jacks to block the rotor. 
 Only three blocks are required for trisector air preheaters. Leave jacks or rams in place to assist with 
 removal of blocks after support bearing has been inspected or replaced.
 Proceed with inspection or replacement of support bearing following 
 procedure noted on
 OM-2258/1 or OM-2258/1/sm.
